title: Benny Waters as a tenor soloist
summary: They place Benny Waters, who came from Baltimore, in the order of early tenor players; Dance thinks he was a section man.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: But I was thinking, now, if you take
that beginning. There's Hawk. There's you and Prince.
Now, okay, you're really like the first three, I reckon, aren't you?
Who else was playing tenor. Was Stump Evans --
No, Stump never did get to New York.
No, but I mean I'm thinking more or less in the chronological order of the way this thing came out, so I mean we'll say Hawk's first. Now then you and Prince.
Then was Benny Waters, [without] taking his place. He came in from Maryland, Baltimore, to New York, and he was working down at -- He's still in Paris now doing good. He was -- came to --
But he was never really much of a soloist. He usually --
Yeah, he was a good soloist.
Yes, he was. He didn't care about nobody.
Well, I always thought he was like a section man in those days.
